86: static void pwc_rx(const void *raw)
87: {
88:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
89:   struct pwc_message message;
90:   unsigned int next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
91:   if (next == g_tail || bytes == NULL)
92:     {
93:       return;
94:     }
95:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
96:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
97:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
98:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
99:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
100:   g_head = next;
101:   nxsem_post(&g_pwc_sem);
102: }
103: 
104: static int pwc_worker(int argc, char **argv)
105: {
106:   (void)argc;
107:   (void)argv;
108:   g_worker_ready = true;
109:   nxsem_post(&g_worker_sem);
110:   for (;;)
111:     {
112:       struct pwc_message message;
113:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_pwc_sem);
114:       message = g_queue[g_tail];
115:       g_tail = (g_tail + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
116:       /* Hardware power/clock actions stay in this thread, never in IRQ. */
117:       switch (message.header & 0xffu)
118:         {
119:           case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
120:             /* The unmodified AVDK SMP firmware returns the requested ON/OFF
121:              * state in param1. It does not expose the PSRAM driver result or
122:              * detected capacity, so AP validates its configured regions with
123:              * the non-destructive boundary probe before creating allocators.
124:              */
125: 
126:             g_psram_power_state = message.param1;
127:             if (g_psram_power_waiting)
128:               {
129:                 g_psram_power_waiting = false;
130:                 nxsem_post(&g_psram_power_sem);
131:               }
132:             break;
133: 
134: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
135:           case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
136:             if (message.param1 == 0u)
137:               {
138:                 (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
139:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
140:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
141:                   bk7258_psram_heap_used(), 0);
142:               }
143:             else if (message.param1 == PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF)
144:               {
145:                 /* This CP notification is sent after physical power-down. */
146: 
147:                 bk7258_psram_power_lost();
148:               }
149:             break;
150: 
151:           case PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD:
152:             bk7258_psram_dump();
153:             break;
154: 
155:           case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
156:             {
157:               int ret = bk7258_psram_shutdown();
158: 
159:               (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
160:                 PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD, PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
161:                 ret == 0 ? PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH :
162:                            PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT, 0);
163:             }
164:             break;
165: #endif
166: 
167:           default:
168:             break;
169:         }
170:     }
171:   return 0;
172: }

113: static int ipc_heartbeat_timeout(void)
114: {
115: 	u32   cur_time;
116: 
117: 	cur_time = (u32)rtos_get_time();
118: 
119: 	if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
120: 	{
121: 		return 0;
122: 	}
123: 	if((cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING) || (cpu_x_dump != 0))
124: 	{
125: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = cur_time;
126: 		return 0;
127: 	}
128: 
129: 	if(cur_time >= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)
130: 	{
131: 		cur_time -= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp;
132: 	}
133: 	else
134: 	{
135: 		cur_time += (~(cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)) + 1;  // wrap around.
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	if(cur_time < HB_TIMEOUT_MS)
139: 	{
140: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
141: 		return 0;
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	if (bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_get(PM_DEV_ID_DEFAULT))
145: 	{
146: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
147: 		bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_clear(PM_DEV_ID_DEFAULT);
148: 		return 0;
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	if(s_mb_ipc_work_state == MB_IPC_EXIT_LV)
152: 	{
153: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
154: 		s_mb_ipc_work_state = MB_IPC_WORKING;
155: 		return 0;
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	return 1;

219: static void mb_ipc_task( void *para )
220: {
221: 	bk_err_t	ret_val;
222: 	u32    events;
223: 	u32    check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
224: 
225: 	mb_ipc_init_lv_callback();
226: 
227: 	ret_val = rtos_init_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event);
228: 
229: 	if(ret_val != BK_OK)
230: 	{
231: 		rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
232: 		return;
233: 	}
234: 
235: 	while(1)
236: 	{
237: 		events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_ALL_FLAGS, true, check_time);
238: 
239: 		if(events == 0)
240: 		{
241: 			// timeout, so check heartbeat.
242: 			events = MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG;
243: 		}
244: 
245: 		if(events & MB_IPC_STOP_CORE_FLAG)  // process this event at first!!!!
246: 		{
247: 			if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
248: 			{
249: 				events = 0;  // clear all events.
250: 			}
251: 		}
252: 
253: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)
254: 		{
255: 			u8   retry_cnt = 0;
256: 
257: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
258: 			{
259: 				ipc_heartbeat_timeout();
260: 
261: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)
262: 				{
263: 					if(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
264: 					{
265: 						cpu_x_state = CORE_POWER_ON;
266: 						break;  // cpu1 power on.
267: 					}
268: 				}
269: 				else
270: 				{
271: 					if( retry_cnt > 3)
272: 					{
273: 						BK_DUMP_OUT("IPC retry to start core%d, retry_cnt:%d\r\n", cpu_x_id, retry_cnt);
274: 						// restart_cpu_x();
275: 						break;
276: 					}
277: 					else
278: 					{
279: 						events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG, true, 2000);//2s
280: 					}
281: 				}
282: 
283: 				retry_cnt++;
284: 			}
285: 
286: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
287: 		}
288: 
289: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
290: 		{
291: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())
292: 			{
293: 				BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC[%d]heartbeat timeout %d,%d\r\n",cpu_x_id,cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp,(u32)rtos_get_time());
294: 				/*when cpu1 heartbeat timeout, then system reboot*/
295: 				cpu_x_heartbeat_timeout = 1;
296: 				ap_console_bridge_link_down();
297: 				BK_ASSERT(false);
298: 			}
299: 		}
300: 
301: 		if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
302: 		{
303: 			check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
304: 		}
305: 		else
306: 		{
307: 			check_time = HB_TIMEOUT_MS;
308: 		}
309: 	}
310: }

<content>
1: # Beken AVDK 覆盖与构建基线
2: 
3: 本目录保存 BK7258 OpenVela 最终固件构建所需的 Beken AVDK 覆盖文件，并作为
4: 多人协作时 `bk_avdk_smp` 修改的同步记录。不要只修改工作区中的
5: `~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp`；可复现修改必须同时更新本目录及本文档。
6: 
7: ## 1. 当前覆盖文件
8: 
9: | 比赛仓权威副本 | `bk_avdk_smp` 目标文件 | 作用 |
10: | --- | --- | --- |
11: | `cp/components/bk_cli/cli_main.c` | `cp/components/bk_cli/cli_main.c` | 注册 `ap_console` CLI 命令 |
12: | `cp/components/bk_cli/shell_task.c` | `cp/components/bk_cli/shell_task.c` | UART0 CP_CLI/AP_CONSOLE owner 状态机、延迟切换和退出转义 |
13: | `cp/include/components/ap_console_bridge.h` | `cp/include/components/ap_console_bridge.h` | CP UART0 bridge 模式、写入和统计接口 |
14: | `cp/include/components/shell_task.h` | `cp/include/components/shell_task.h` | shell 与 bridge 的切换/链路事件接口 |
15: | `cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h` | `cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h` | transport event、诊断和 poll 接口 |
16: | `cp/include/driver/mb_uart_driver.h` | `cp/include/driver/mb_uart_driver.h` | MB_UART link event、状态和 poll 接口 |
17: | `cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c` | MB_UART0 唯一 owner、LOG/RAW RX、1024 B TX ring 和 worker |
18: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c` | 完整 ACK 匹配、timeout/reset、probe 和诊断 |
19: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c` | IPC power-up ready 门禁事件 |
20: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c` | heartbeat/reset/down 自动回退事件 |
21: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_uart_driver.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_uart_driver.c` | 严格 DATA/STATE 校验、ACK 后推进和 link event |
22: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c` | command/ACK/reset/sync 分离稳定 slot |
23: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.h` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.h` | 稳定 slot 完成和 quarantine 接口 |
24: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c` | RX 资源门禁、FIFO poll 和 destination count |
25: | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.h` | `cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.h` | MBOX0 poll、ready callback 和 FIFO count API |
26: | `cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c` | `cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c` | PWC boot-ready 门禁事件 |
27: | `projects/app_ab/partitions/bk7258/ram_regions.csv` | `projects/app_ab/partitions/bk7258/ram_regions.csv` | BK7258 640 KiB Share SRAM 和 16 MiB PSRAM 布局 |
28: 
29: UART0 bridge 保持 `MB_UART0` 唯一初始化 owner。AP 输出 LOG 模式保留 `ap0:`
30: 前缀、50 ms 半行刷新和有限重试；RAW 模式不改写字节。PC 到 AP 输入使用
31: 1024 B 有界 ring 和部分写 worker，所有物理 UART0 输出仍经 shell queue 串行化。
32: 
33: `ram_regions.csv`采用原厂 `lvgl/img_decode`、`lvgl/freetype_font` 的 16 MiB
34: 七区域布局：
35: 
36: ```text
37: 0x60000000..0x60700000  四个媒体 slab，共 7 MiB
38: 0x60700000..0x60720000  CP PSRAM heap，128 KiB
39: 0x60720000..0x60a00000  AP PSRAM heap，2.875 MiB
40: 0x60a00000..0x61000000  AP PSRAM section，6 MiB
41: ```
42: 
43: ## 2. 同步到 SMP 工作树
44: 
45: 从工作区根目录执行：
46: 
47: ```bash
48: mirror=contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp

72: 同步后必须逐字节检查：
73: 
74: ```bash

99: 
100: ## 3. 正确构建链条
101: 
102: 最终固件链条固定为：
103: 
104: ```text
105: OpenVela nuttx.bin
106:   -> bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
107:   -> EXTERNAL_AP_BIN
108:   -> package/tmp/app1.bin
109:   -> package/all-app.bin
110: 
111: Armino CP app.bin + Beken bootloader.bin
112:   ---------------------------------------> package/all-app.bin
113: ```
114: 
115: 修改以下任一输入后，不得直接做 SMP 增量构建：
116: 
117: - `ram_regions.csv`
118: - AP/CP `config`
119: - Kconfig 默认值
120: - 分区生成脚本
121: - SoC 链接脚本
122: 
123: 原因是顶层 `partitions/ram_regions.h` 可以先更新，而 AP/CP CMake 构建目录中的
124: `armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv`、生成头和预处理链接脚本仍可能保留旧值。
125: 这会形成顶层 16 MiB、核内仍 8 MiB 的不一致产物。
126: 
127: 先构建 OpenVela AP，并将输入放到 SMP 工作树：
128: 
129: ```bash
130: cd ~/vela_competition/contest
131: ./build.sh \
132:   vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh \
133:   -e -Werror --cmake -j8
134: 
135: cp \
136:   cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin \
137:   ~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
138: ```
139: 
140: 然后执行项目级 clean 和容器内完整构建：
141: 
142: ```bash
143: cd ~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp
144: make -C projects/app_ab clean
145: 
146: podman run --rm \
147:   --userns=keep-id \
148:   -v "$PWD:/armino" \
149:   -w /armino \
150:   localhost/bekencorp/armino-idk:1.5 \
151:   make -C projects/app_ab bk7258 \
152:   SDK_DIR=/armino \
153:   EXTERNAL_AP_BIN=/armino/build/openvela-ap.bin
154: ```
155: 
156: `make -C projects/app_ab clean`只删除`projects/app_ab/build`，不会删除
157: `build/openvela-ap.bin`。仅安装 Podman 时不要使用内部调用 Docker 的`dbuild.sh`。
158: 
159: ## 4. 构建验收
160: 
161: 以下文件必须都反映同一份 16 MiB 布局：
162: 
163: ```text
164: projects/app_ab/partitions/bk7258/ram_regions.csv
165: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/partitions/ram_regions.h
166: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv
167: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258_ap/armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv
168: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/bk7258/bk7258_out.ld
169: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258_ap/armino/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap_out.ld
170: ```
171: 
172: 关键值应为：
173: 
174: ```text
175: CONFIG_PSRAM_CAPACITY          0x01000000
176: CP_PSRAM_HEAP                 0x60700000 + 0x00020000
177: AP_PSRAM_HEAP                 0x60720000 + 0x002e0000
178: AP_PSRAM_SECTION              0x60a00000 + 0x00600000
179: PSRAM 最终边界                0x61000000
180: ```
181: 
182: 外部 AP 输入和最终打包输入必须完全一致：
183: 
184: ```bash
185: sha256sum \
186:   ~/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin \
187:   build/openvela-ap.bin \
188:   projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/tmp/app1.bin
189: 
190: cmp -s \
191:   build/openvela-ap.bin \
192:   projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/tmp/app1.bin
193: ```
194: 
195: 检查最终产物：
196: 
197: ```text
198: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin
199: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/app_ab_crc.rbl
200: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/build_summary.txt
201: ```
202: 
203: `build_summary.txt`中的 AP 内存统计来自 Armino AP 占位镜像，只用于检查生成的
204: 内存区域边界；它不代表最终打包的 OpenVela AP 静态占用。OpenVela AP 的静态
205: 内存应以 `nuttx.map`或`System.map`为准。
206: 
207: ## 5. OpenVela PSRAM 接入状态
208: 
209: OpenVela AP侧已经完成以下代码和离线构建基线：
210: 
211: - 精确16 MiB、RW/XN/non-cacheable MPU映射。
212: - `0x60720000..0x609fffff`独立AP PSRAM heap。
213: - USER/AUDIO/ENCODE/DISPLAY四个独立媒体pool。
214: - 明确排除`0x60700000..0x6071ffff` CP heap的地址检查。
215: - AP owner区域保存/恢复型alias probe，包含4/8/12 MiB测试点。
216: - 当前SMP协议兼容的`0x7/0x8/0x9/0xa`PWC处理和PSRAM_REQUIRED ready门禁。
217: - `0x60a00000..0x60ffffff`静态section链接保留；reset copy/clear未实现前强制0 B。
218: 
219: 当前CP协议不通过`0xc`或其他命令暴露PSRAM initialized、device ID和actual capacity。
220: `0x7`响应只回显ON/OFF状态，不能单独证明PHY初始化成功或器件为16 MiB。因此当前
221: alias probe是临时运行时门禁，不能替代CP status协议扩展和整颗器件实板测试。
222: 
223: 当前OpenVela构建和最终打包使用同一个 AP 输入：
224: 
225: ```text
226: cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin
227: bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
228: bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/tmp/app1.bin
229: SHA256 133cf4b8e54075bfac6ce70bfc1e042888ce22c1a64cc65742a7ee95653d8b6e
230: ```
231: 
232: 最终包已使用上述 OpenVela AP 重新生成：
233: 
234: ```text
235: all-app.bin SHA256
236: 93e540db51f262fd846620ca4257dfefbe5025f796466ab3fcf9fb6a29c51fe0
237: 
238: app_ab_crc.rbl SHA256
239: 447f5eca7c0b3dafd6b47223aa1c7327478a9d9f9ca0db030104e5829c44a20c
240: ```
241: 
242: 除AP/CP `-Werror`编译、最终打包和AP输入一致性外，当前固件已在实板验证UART0
243: 双向桥、IPC/PWC ready、heartbeat、PSRAM、NSH交互、CLE方向键与控制键、TTY
244: `Ctrl-C`信号以及AP控制台退出转义。
245: 
246: ## 6. 协作约束
247: 
248: - 不提交 `projects/app_ab/build`、顶层 `build`或`__pycache__`。
249: - 不把构建生成的完整 AP/CP配置误当作最小项目配置同步回比赛仓。
250: - SMP 工作树可能包含其他成员的未提交修改；同步覆盖前先检查`git diff`。
251: - 新增任何 SMP 源码修改时，在本目录保留对应路径的权威副本，并更新上面的
252:   覆盖表、构建步骤和验收项。
253: - 当前阶段已完成OpenVela AP allocator、四个媒体pool和空静态PSRAM section的代码
254:   接入与离线构建；尚未完成CP ID/容量query、NSH压力测试、DMA/media lease、实板
255:   验证和最终包重打包。
256: 
257: ## 7. UART0 Mailbox V2 使用和边界
258: 
259: CP 启动后默认 owner 为 `CP_CLI`。只有 MB_UART0 STATE 成功 ACK、IPC power-up 和
260: PWC boot-ready 三个条件同时成立，且`bk_mb_uart_write_ready()`非零时，
261: `ap_console open`才允许进入。heartbeat timeout、AP reset/power-off 和 Mailbox
262: reset/timeout都会清除门禁并请求回退到CP CLI。使用方式：
263: 
264: ```text
265: ap_console status
266: ap_console open
267: <RAW AP NSH interaction>
268: <press Ctrl-], release it, then press .>
269: ap_console status
270: ```
271: 
272: `open`在当前 CP CLI 响应经 UART TX-complete 后生效，并清 CP parser 和 UART RX；
273: RAW 模式不添加前缀。退出时按下`Ctrl-]`、松开，再按`.`；该转义不依赖行首状态。
274: 链路 reset/timeout/down 时自动清理
275: 未发送输入并回到 `CP_CLI`。`status`输出 owner/link/mode、bridge ring、MB_UART 状态、

45: /****************************************************************************
46:  * Name: nxsig_nanosleep
47:  *
48:  * Description:
49:  *   The nxsig_nanosleep() function causes the current thread to be
50:  *   suspended from execution until either the time interval specified by
51:  *   the rqtp argument has elapsed or a signal is delivered to the calling
52:  *   thread and its action is to invoke a signal-catching function or to
53:  *   terminate the process. The suspension time may be longer than requested
54:  *   because the argument value is rounded up to an integer multiple of the
55:  *   sleep resolution or because of the scheduling of other activity by the
56:  *   system. But, except for the case of being interrupted by a signal, the
57:  *   suspension time will not be less than the time specified by rqtp, as
58:  *   measured by the system clock, CLOCK_REALTIME.
59:  *
60:  *   The use of the nxsig_nanosleep() function has no effect on the action
61:  *   or blockage of any signal.
62:  *
63:  * Input Parameters:
64:  *   rqtp - The amount of time to be suspended from execution.
65:  *   rmtp - If the rmtp argument is non-NULL, the timespec structure
66:  *          referenced by it is updated to contain the amount of time
67:  *          remaining in the interval (the requested time minus the time
68:  *          actually slept)
69:  *
70:  * Returned Value:
71:  *   If the nxsig_nanosleep() function returns because the requested time
72:  *   has elapsed, its return value is zero.
73:  *
74:  *   If the nxsig_nanosleep() function returns because it has been
75:  *   interrupted by a signal, the function returns a negated errno value
76:  *   indicate the interruption. If the rmtp argument is non-NULL, the
77:  *   timespec structure referenced by it is updated to contain the amount
78:  *   of time remaining in the interval (the requested time minus the time
79:  *   actually slept). If the rmtp argument is NULL, the remaining time is
80:  *   not returned.
81:  *
82:  *   If nxsig_nanosleep() fails, it returns a negated errno indicating the
83:  *   cause of the failure. The nxsig_nanosleep() function will fail if:
84:  *
85:  *     EINTR - The nxsig_nanosleep() function was interrupted by a signal.
86:  *     EINVAL - The rqtp argument specified a nanosecond value less than
87:  *       zero or greater than or equal to 1000 million.
88:  *     ENOSYS - The nxsig_nanosleep() function is not supported by this
89:  *       implementation.
90:  *
91:  ****************************************************************************/
92: 
93: int nxsig_nanosleep(FAR const struct timespec *rqtp,
94:                     FAR struct timespec *rmtp)
95: {
96:   int ret;
97: 
98:   ret = nxsig_clockwait(CLOCK_REALTIME, 0, rqtp, rmtp);
99: 
100:   return ret == -EAGAIN ? 0 : ret;
101: }
102: 
103: /****************************************************************************
104:  * Name: clock_nanosleep
105:  *
106:  * Description:
107:  *   If the flag TIMER_ABSTIME is not set in the flags argument, the
108:  *   clock_nanosleep() function will cause the current thread to be suspended
109:  *   from execution until either the time interval specified by the rqtp
110:  *   argument has elapsed, or a signal is delivered to the calling thread
111:  *   and its action is to invoke a signal-catching function, or the process
112:  *   is terminated. The clock used to measure the time will be the clock
113:  *   specified by clock_id.
114:  *
115:  *   If the flag TIMER_ABSTIME is set in the flags argument, the
116:  *   clock_nanosleep() function will cause the current thread to be
117:  *   suspended from execution until either the time value of the clock
118:  *   specified by clock_id reaches the absolute time specified by the rqtp
119:  *   argument, or a signal is delivered to the calling thread and its action
120:  *   is to invoke a signal-catching function, or the process is terminated.
121:  *   If, at the time of the call, the time value specified by rqtp is less
122:  *   than or equal to the time value of the specified clock, then
123:  *   clock_nanosleep() will return immediately and the calling process will
124:  *   not be suspended.
125:  *
126:  *   The suspension time caused by this function may be longer than requested
127:  *   because the argument value is rounded up to an integer multiple of the
128:  *   sleep resolution, or because of the scheduling of other activity by the
129:  *   system. But, except for the case of being interrupted by a signal, the
130:  *   suspension time for the relative clock_nanosleep() function (that is,
131:  *   with the TIMER_ABSTIME flag not set) will not be less than the time
132:  *   interval specified by rqtp, as measured by the corresponding clock. The
133:  *   suspension for the absolute clock_nanosleep() function (that is, with
134:  *   the TIMER_ABSTIME flag set) will be in effect at least until the value
135:  *   of the corresponding clock reaches the absolute time specified by rqtp,
136:  *   except for the case of being interrupted by a signal.
137:  *
138:  *   The use of the clock_nanosleep() function will have no effect on the
139:  *   action or blockage of any signal.
140:  *
141:  *   The clock_nanosleep() function will fail if the clock_id argument refers
142:  *   to the CPU-time clock of the calling thread. It is unspecified whether
143:  *   clock_id values of other CPU-time clocks are allowed.
144:  *
145:  * Input Parameters:
146:  *   clockid - The clock to use to interpret the absolute time
147:  *   flags   - Open flags.  TIMER_ABSTIME  is the only supported flag.
148:  *   rqtp    - The amount of time to be suspended from execution.
149:  *   rmtp    - If the rmtp argument is non-NULL, the timespec structure
150:  *             referenced by it is updated to contain the amount of time
151:  *             remaining in the interval (the requested time minus the time
152:  *             actually slept)
153:  *
154:  * Returned Value:
155:  *   If the clock_nanosleep() function returns because the requested time has
156:  *   elapsed, its return value is zero.
157:  *
158:  *   If the clock_nanosleep() function returns because it has been
159:  *   interrupted by a signal, the function returns a value of -1 and sets
160:  *   errno to indicate the interruption. If the rmtp argument is non-NULL,
161:  *   the timespec structure referenced by it is updated to contain the amount
162:  *   of time remaining in the interval (the requested time minus the time
163:  *   actually slept). If the rmtp argument is NULL, the remaining time is not
164:  *   returned.
165:  *
166:  *   If clock_nanosleep() fails, it returns a value of errno. The
167:  *   clock_nanosleep() function will fail if:
168:  *
169:  *     EINTR - The clock_nanosleep() function was interrupted by a signal.
170:  *     EINVAL - The rqtp argument specified a nanosecond value less than
171:  *       zero or greater than or equal to 1000 million. Or the clockid that
172:  *       does not specify a known clock.
173:  *     ENOSYS - The clock_nanosleep() function is not supported by this
174:  *       implementation.
175:  *
176:  ****************************************************************************/
177: 
178: int clock_nanosleep(clockid_t clockid, int flags,
179:                     FAR const struct timespec *rqtp,
180:                     FAR struct timespec *rmtp)
181: {
182:   int ret = EINVAL;
183: 
184:   /* clock_nanosleep() is a cancellation point */
185: 
186:   enter_cancellation_point();
187: 
188:   if (clockid >= CLOCK_REALTIME && clockid <= CLOCK_BOOTTIME)
189:     {
190:       /* Just a wrapper around nxsig_clockwait() */
191: 
192:       ret = nxsig_clockwait(clockid, flags, rqtp, rmtp);
193: 
194:       /* Check if nxsig_clockwait() succeeded */
195: 
196:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
197:         {
198:           ret = OK;
199:         }
200:       else if (ret < 0)
201:         {
202:           /* If not return the errno */
203: 
204:           ret = -ret;
205:         }
206:     }
207: 
208:   leave_cancellation_point();
209:   return ret;
210: }

401: 
402:   /* Get the elapsed time since power up (in milliseconds).  This is a

428: 
429:       rtc_diff->tv_sec = 0;
430:       rtc_diff->tv_nsec = 0;
431:     }
432:   else
433:     {
434:       /* Output difference between time at entry and new current time. */
435: 
436:       clock_timespec_subtract(&rtc_time, &curr_ts, rtc_diff);
437: 
438:       /* Add the sleep time to correct system timer */
439: 
440:       clock_t diff_ticks = SEC2TICK(rtc_diff->tv_sec) +
441:                            NSEC2TICK(rtc_diff->tv_nsec);
442: 
443:       flags = write_seqlock_irqsave(&g_system_tick_lock);
444:       g_system_ticks += diff_ticks;
445:       write_sequnlock_irqrestore(&g_system_tick_lock, flags);

68: static uint32_t update_timeout(uint32_t timeout)
69: {
70:   struct timer_status_s status;
71: 
72:   /* Don't need critical section here
73:    * since caller already do it for us
74:    */
75: 
76:   TIMER_TICK_GETSTATUS(g_timer.lower, &status);
77:   if (g_timer.next_interval)
78:     {
79:       /* If the timer interrupt is in the process,
80:        * let the callback return the right interval.
81:        */
82: 
83:       *g_timer.next_interval = timeout;
84:     }
85:   else if (timeout != status.timeleft)
86:     {
87:       /* Otherwise, update the timeout directly. */
88: 
89:       TIMER_TICK_SETTIMEOUT(g_timer.lower, timeout);
90:       g_timer.timebase += status.timeout - status.timeleft;
91:     }
92: 
93:   return status.timeleft;
94: }

97: static uint64_t current_usec(void)
98: {
99:   struct timer_status_s status;
100:   clock_t timebase;
101: 
102:   do
103:     {
104:       timebase = g_timer.timebase;
105:       TIMER_GETSTATUS(g_timer.lower, &status);
106:     }
107:   while (timebase != g_timer.timebase);
108: 
109:   return TICK2USEC(timebase) + (status.timeout - status.timeleft);
110: }

121: static void udelay_coarse(useconds_t microseconds)
122: {

125:   /* We'll do this a little at a time because we expect that the
126:    * CONFIG_BOARD_LOOPSPERUSEC is very inaccurate during to truncation in
127:    * the divisions of its calculation.  We'll use the largest values that
128:    * we can in order to prevent significant error buildup in the loops.
129:    */
130: 
131:   while (microseconds > 1000)
132:     {
133:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_BOARD_LOOPSPERMSEC; i++)
134:         {
135:         }
136: 
137:       microseconds -= 1000;
138:     }
139: 
140:   while (microseconds > 100)
141:     {
142:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_BOARD_LOOPSPER100USEC; i++)
143:         {
144:         }
145: 
146:       microseconds -= 100;
147:     }
148: 
149:   while (microseconds > 10)

151:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_BOARD_LOOPSPER10USEC; i++)
152:         {
153:         }
154: 
155:       microseconds -= 10;

158:   while (microseconds > 0)

162:         }

246: void weak_function up_timer_getmask(FAR clock_t *mask)

232:  *   rmtp - If the rmtp argument is non-NULL, the timespec structure
233:  *          referenced by it is updated to contain the amount of time
234:  *          remaining in the interval (the requested time minus the time
235:  *          actually slept)
236:  *
237:  * Returned Value:
238:  *   This is an internal OS interface and should not be used by applications.
239:  *   A negated errno value is returned on failure.
240:  *
241:  *   EAGAIN - wait time is zero.
242:  *   EINTR  - The wait was interrupted by an unblocked, caught signal.
243:  *
244:  * Notes:
245:  *  This function should be called with critical section set.
246:  *
247:  ****************************************************************************/

249: int nxsig_clockwait(int clockid, int flags,
250:                     FAR const struct timespec *rqtp,
251:                     FAR struct timespec *rmtp)
252: {
253:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
254:   irqstate_t iflags;
255:   clock_t expect = 0u;
256:   clock_t stop   = 0u;
257:   int ret = OK;
258: 
259:   if (rqtp && (rqtp->tv_nsec < 0 || rqtp->tv_nsec >= 1000000000))
260:     {
261:       ret = -EINVAL;
262:     }
263: 
264:   /* If rqtp is zero, yield CPU and return
265:    * Notice: The behavior of sleep(0) is not defined in POSIX, so there are
266:    * different implementations:
267:    * 1. In Linux, nanosleep(0) will call schedule() to yield CPU:
268:    *    https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/latest/source/kernel/time/
269:    *    hrtimer.c#L2038
270:    * 2. In BSD, nanosleep(0) will return immediately:
271:    *    https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/
272:    *    475fa89800086718bd9249fd4dc3f862549f1f78/crypto/openssh/
273:    *    openbsd-compat/bsd-misc.c#L243
274:    */
275: 
276:   else if (rqtp && rqtp->tv_sec == 0 && rqtp->tv_nsec == 0)
277:     {
278:       sched_yield();
279:       ret = -EAGAIN;
280:     }
281: 
282: #ifdef CONFIG_CANCELLATION_POINTS
283:   /* nxsig_clockwait() is not a cancellation point, but it may be called
284:    * from a cancellation point.  So if a cancellation is pending, we
285:    * must exit immediately without waiting.
286:    */
287: 
288:   else if (check_cancellation_point())
289:     {
290:       /* If there is a pending cancellation, then do not perform
291:        * the wait.  Exit now with ECANCELED.
292:        */
293: 
294:       ret = -ECANCELED;
295:     }
296: #endif
297:   else
298:     {
299:       iflags = enter_critical_section();
300: 
301:       if (rqtp)
302:         {
303:           /* Start the watchdog timer */
304: 
305:           if ((flags & TIMER_ABSTIME) == 0)
306:             {
307:               expect = clock_delay2abstick(clock_time2ticks(rqtp));
308:               wd_start_abstick(&rtcb->waitdog, expect,
309:                                nxsig_timeout, (uintptr_t)rtcb);
310:             }
311:           else if (clockid == CLOCK_REALTIME)
312:             {
313:               wd_start_realtime(&rtcb->waitdog, rqtp,
314:                                 nxsig_timeout, (uintptr_t)rtcb);
315:             }
316:           else
317:             {
318:               wd_start_abstime(&rtcb->waitdog, rqtp,
319:                                nxsig_timeout, (uintptr_t)rtcb);
320:             }
321:         }
322: 
323:       /* Remove the tcb task from the ready-to-run list. */
324: 
325:       nxsched_remove_self(rtcb);
326: 
327:       /* Add the task to the specified blocked task list */
328: 
329:       rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_WAIT_SIG;
330:       dq_addlast((FAR dq_entry_t *)rtcb, &g_waitingforsignal);
331: 
332:       /* Now, perform the context switch if one is needed */
333: 
334:       nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
335: 
336:       /* We no longer need the watchdog */
337: 
338:       if (rqtp)
339:         {
340:           wd_cancel(&rtcb->waitdog);
341:           stop = clock_systime_ticks();
342:         }
343: 
344:       leave_critical_section(iflags);
345: 
346:       if (rqtp && rmtp && expect)
347:         {
348:           clock_ticks2time(rmtp, expect > stop ? expect - stop : 0u);
349:         }
350:     }
351: 
352:   return ret;
353: }

241: /****************************************************************************
242:  * Name: wd_start_abstick
243:  *
244:  * Description:
245:  *   This function adds a watchdog timer to the active timer queue.  The
246:  *   specified watchdog function at 'wdentry' will be called from the
247:  *   interrupt level after the specified number of ticks has reached.
248:  *   Watchdog timers may be started from the interrupt level.
249:  *
250:  *   Watchdog timers execute in the address environment that was in effect
251:  *   when wd_start() is called.
252:  *
253:  *   Watchdog timers execute only once.
254:  *
255:  *   To replace either the timeout delay or the function to be executed,
256:  *   call wd_start again with the same wdog; only the most recent wdStart()
257:  *   on a given watchdog ID has any effect.
258:  *
259:  * Input Parameters:
260:  *   wdog     - Watchdog ID
261:  *   ticks    - Absolute time in clock ticks
262:  *   wdentry  - Function to call on timeout
263:  *   arg      - Parameter to pass to wdentry.
264:  *
265:  *   NOTE:  The parameter must be of type wdparm_t.
266:  *
267:  * Returned Value:
268:  *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is return to
269:  *   indicate the nature of any failure.
270:  *
271:  * Assumptions:
272:  *   The watchdog routine runs in the context of the timer interrupt handler
273:  *   and is subject to all ISR restrictions.
274:  *
275:  ****************************************************************************/
276: 
277: int wd_start_abstick(FAR struct wdog_s *wdog, clock_t ticks,
278:                      wdentry_t wdentry, wdparm_t arg)
279: {
280:   int ret = -EINVAL;
281:   irqstate_t flags;
282:   bool reassess = false;
283: 
284:   /* Verify the wdog and setup parameters */
285: 
286:   if (wdog != NULL && wdentry != NULL)
287:     {
288:       /* NOTE:  There is a race condition here... the caller may receive
289:        * the watchdog between the time that wd_start_abstick is called and
290:        * the critical section is established.
291:        */
292: 
293:       flags = enter_critical_section();
294: 
295:       /* If the wdog is canceling, restarting the wdog is not allowed. */
296: 
297: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
298:       /* We need to reassess timer if the watchdog
299:        * list head has changed.
300:        */
301: 
302:       if (WDOG_ISACTIVE(wdog))
303:         {
304:           reassess |= list_is_head(&g_wdactivelist, &wdog->node);
305:           list_delete(&wdog->node);
306:         }
307: 
308:       reassess |= wd_insert(wdog, ticks, wdentry, arg);
309: 
310:       /* If wd_start is called in the expiration callbacks,
311:        * the reassess proccess is disabled.
312:        */
313: 
314:       reassess &= !g_wdtimernested;
315: 
316:       leave_critical_section(flags);
317: 
318:       if (reassess)
319:         {
320:           /* Resume the interval timer that will generate the next
321:            * interval event. If the timer at the head of the list
322:            * changed, then this will pick that new delay.
323:            */
324: 
325:           nxsched_reassess_timer();
326:         }
327: #else
328:       UNUSED(reassess);
329: 
330:       /* Check if the watchdog has been started. If so, delete it. */
331: 
332:       if (WDOG_ISACTIVE(wdog))
333:         {
334:           list_delete(&wdog->node);
335:         }
336: 
337:       wd_insert(wdog, ticks, wdentry, arg);
338: 
339:       leave_critical_section(flags);
340: #endif

349: /****************************************************************************
350:  * Name: wd_start
351:  *
352:  * Description:
353:  *   This function adds a watchdog timer to the active timer queue.  The
354:  *   specified watchdog function at 'wdentry' will be called from the
355:  *   interrupt level after the specified number of ticks has elapsed.
356:  *   Watchdog timers may be started from the interrupt level.
357:  *
358:  *   Watchdog timers execute in the address environment that was in effect
359:  *   when wd_start() is called.
360:  *
361:  *   Watchdog timers execute only once.
362:  *
363:  *   To replace either the timeout delay or the function to be executed,
364:  *   call wd_start again with the same wdog; only the most recent wdStart()
365:  *   on a given watchdog ID has any effect.
366:  *
367:  * Input Parameters:
368:  *   wdog     - Watchdog ID
369:  *   delay    - Delay count in clock ticks
370:  *   wdentry  - Function to call on timeout
371:  *   arg      - Parameter to pass to wdentry
372:  *
373:  *   NOTE:  The parameter must be of type wdparm_t.
374:  *
375:  * Returned Value:
376:  *   Zero (OK) is returned on success; a negated errno value is return to
377:  *   indicate the nature of any failure.
378:  *
379:  * Assumptions:
380:  *   The watchdog routine runs in the context of the timer interrupt handler
381:  *   and is subject to all ISR restrictions.
382:  *
383:  ****************************************************************************/
384: 
385: int wd_start(FAR struct wdog_s *wdog, clock_t delay,
386:              wdentry_t wdentry, wdparm_t arg)
387: {
388:   int ret = -EINVAL;
389: 
390:   /* Ensure delay is within the range the wdog can handle. */
391: 
392:   if (delay <= WDOG_MAX_DELAY)
393:     {
394:       ret = wd_start_abstick(wdog, clock_delay2abstick(delay), wdentry, arg);
395:     }
396: 
397:   return ret;
398: }

544: /****************************************************************************
545:  * Name:  nxsched_reassess_timer
546:  *
547:  * Description:
548:  *   It is necessary to re-assess the timer interval in several
549:  *   circumstances:
550:  *
551:  *   - If the watchdog at the head of the expiration list changes (or if its
552:  *     delay changes.  This can occur as a consequence of the actions of
553:  *     wd_start() or wd_cancel().
554:  *   - When pre-emption is re-enabled.  A previous time slice may have
555:  *     expired while pre-emption was enabled and now needs to be executed.
556:  *
557:  *   In the original design, it was also planned that
558:  *   nxsched_reassess_timer() be called whenever there was a change at the
559:  *   head of the ready-to-run list.  That call was intended to establish a
560:  *   new time-slice for the newly activated task or to stop the timer if
561:  *   time-slicing is no longer needed.  However, it turns out that that
562:  *   solution is too fragile:  The system is too vulnerable at the time
563:  *   that the ready-to-run list is modified in order to muck with timers.
564:  *
565:  *   The kludge/work-around is simple to keep the timer running all of the
566:  *   time with an interval of no more than the timeslice interval.  If we
567:  *   do this, then there is really no need to do anything on context
568:  *   switches.
569:  *
570:  * Input Parameters:
571:  *   None
572:  *
573:  * Returned Value:
574:  *   None
575:  *
576:  * Note:
577:  *   This function is called from the critical section
578:  *
579:  ****************************************************************************/
580: 
581: void nxsched_reassess_timer(void)
582: {
583:   clock_t    ticks;
584:   irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
585: 
586:   /* Cancel the timer and get the current time */
587: 
588: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS_ALARM
589:   up_alarm_tick_cancel(&ticks);
590: #else
591:   clock_t elapsed;
592:   up_timer_gettick(&ticks);
593:   up_timer_tick_cancel(&elapsed);
594: #endif
595: 
596:   nxsched_timer_update(ticks, true);
597: 
598:   leave_critical_section(flags);
599: }
600:

602:  * Name:  nxsched_get_next_expired
603:  *
604:  * Description:
605:  *   Get the time remaining until the next timer expiration.
606:  *
607:  * Input Parameters:
608:  *   None
609:  *
610:  * Returned Value:
611:  *   The time remaining until the next timer expiration.
612:  *
613:  * Note:
614:  *   There is two special returned value
615:  *   Zero     : The timer already expired or in processing.
616:  *   CLOCK_MAX: There is no working timer.
617:  *
618:  ****************************************************************************/
619: 
620: clock_t nxsched_get_next_expired(void)
621: {
622:   sclock_t delta;
623:   clock_t ret  = 0;
624:   clock_t intv = atomic_read(&g_timer_interval);
625: 
626:   if (intv == 0)
627:     {
628:       ret = CLOCK_MAX;
629:     }
630:   else
631:     {
632:       delta = get_time_tick() + intv - clock_systime_ticks();
633:       ret   = delta > 0 ? delta : 0;
634:     }
635: 
636:   return ret;
637: }
638: 
639: #endif /* CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS */

98: /****************************************************************************
99:  * Name: wd_expiration
100:  *
101:  * Description:
102:  *   Check if the timer for the watchdog at the head of list is ready to
103:  *   run. If so, remove the watchdog from the list and execute it.
104:  *   Note: This function should always be called in the interrupt context.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   ticks - current time in ticks
108:  *
109:  * Returned Value:
110:  *   None
111:  *
112:  ****************************************************************************/

114: static inline_function clock_t wd_expiration(clock_t ticks)
115: {
116:   FAR struct wdog_s *wdog;
117:   irqstate_t         flags;
118:   wdentry_t          func;
119:   wdparm_t           arg;
120:   clock_t            ret = CLOCK_MAX;
121: 
122:   flags = enter_critical_section();
123: 
124: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
125:   /* Increment the nested watchdog timer count to handle cases where wd_start
126:    * is called in the watchdog callback functions.
127:    */
128: 
129:   g_wdtimernested++;
130: #endif
131: 
132:   /* Process the watchdog at the head of the list as well as any
133:    * other watchdogs that became ready to run at this time
134:    */
135: 
136:   while (!list_is_empty(&g_wdactivelist))
137:     {
138:       wdog = list_first_entry(&g_wdactivelist, struct wdog_s, node);
139: 
140:       /* Check if expected time is expired */
141: 
142:       if (!clock_compare(wdog->expired, ticks))
143:         {
144:           ret = wdog->expired - ticks;
145:           break;
146:         }
147: 
148:       /* Remove the watchdog from the head of the list */
149: 
150:       list_delete(&wdog->node);
151: 
152:       /* Indicate that the watchdog is no longer active. */
153: 
154:       func = wdog->func;
155:       arg = wdog->arg;
156:       wdog->func = NULL;
157: 
158:       /* Execute the watchdog function */
159: 
160:       up_setpicbase(wdog->picbase);
161: 
162:       CALL_FUNC(func, arg);
163:     }
164: 
165: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
166:   /* Decrement the nested watchdog timer count */
167: 
168:   g_wdtimernested--;
169: #endif
170: 
171:   leave_critical_section(flags);
172: 
173:   return ret;
174: }

177:  * Name: wd_insert
178:  *
179:  * Description:
180:  *   Insert the timer into the global list to ensure that
181:  *   the list is sorted in increasing order of expiration absolute time.
182:  *
183:  * Input Parameters:
184:  *   wdog     - Watchdog ID
185:  *   expired  - expired absolute time in clock ticks
186:  *   wdentry  - Function to call on timeout
187:  *   arg      - Parameter to pass to wdentry
188:  *
189:  * Assumptions:
190:  *   wdog and wdentry is not NULL.
191:  *
192:  * Returned Value:
193:  *   Whether the head of the watchdog list has changed.

195:  ****************************************************************************/

197: static inline_function
198: bool wd_insert(FAR struct wdog_s *wdog, clock_t expired,
199:                wdentry_t wdentry, wdparm_t arg)
200: {
201:   FAR struct wdog_s *curr;
202:   FAR struct wdog_s *head;
203: 
204:   /* Traverse the watchdog list */
205: 
206:   head = list_first_entry(&g_wdactivelist, struct wdog_s, node);
207: 
208:   list_for_every_entry(&g_wdactivelist, curr, struct wdog_s, node)
209:     {
210:       /* Until curr->expired has not timed out relative to expired */
211: 
212:       if (!clock_compare(curr->expired, expired))
213:         {
214:           break;
215:         }
216:     }
217: 
218:   /* There are two cases:
219:    * - Traverse to the end, where curr == &g_wdactivelist.
220:    * - Find a curr such that curr->expected has not timed out
221:    * relative to expired.
222:    * In either case 1 or 2, we just insert the wdog before curr.
223:    */
224: 
225:   list_add_before(&curr->node, &wdog->node);
226: 
227:   wdog->func = wdentry;
228:   up_getpicbase(&wdog->picbase);
229:   wdog->arg = arg;
230:   wdog->expired = expired;
231: 
232:   /* Return whether the head of the watchdog list has changed. */
233: 
234:   return head == curr;
235: }

654: static int handle_command(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
655: {
656:   struct ack_slot *slot;
657:   unsigned int rx_index;
658:   uint8_t channel = bk7258_mb_header_channel(message);
659:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
660:   uint8_t ack_flags = 0;
661:   uint8_t state = 0;
662:   int ret = -ENOSYS;
663: 
664:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) == 0)
665:     {
666:       slot = alloc_ack_slot();
667:       if (slot == NULL)
668:         {
669:           g_stats.deferred_command++;
670:           return -EAGAIN;
671:         }
672:     }
673:   else
674:     {
675:       slot = NULL;
676:     }
677: 
678:   if ((control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0 ||
679:       bk7258_mb_header_state(message) != 0 ||
680:       (channel & 0xf0u) != 0x40u)
681:     {
682:       g_stats.bad_header++;
683:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
684:     }
685:   else if ((rx_index = rx_channel_index(channel)) < MB_RX_CHANNEL_COUNT &&
686:            g_rx_callbacks[rx_index] != NULL)
687:     {
688:       ret = g_rx_callbacks[rx_index](message, &ack_flags,
689:                                      g_rx_args[rx_index]);
690:       if (ret < 0)
691:         {
692:           state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
693:         }
694:     }
695:   else if (channel == BK7258_MB_CHAN_PWC_RX && g_pwc_rx != NULL)
696:     {
697:       g_pwc_rx(message);
698:       ret = OK;
699:     }
700:   else
701:     {
702:       g_stats.unsupported++;
703:       state = BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL;
704:     }
705: 
706:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX) != 0)
707:     {
708:       return OK;
709:     }
710: 
711:   memset(&slot->message, 0, sizeof(slot->message));
712:   slot->message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
713:     bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message), state, BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX,
714:     bk7258_mb_header_seq(message), channel);
715:   slot->message.payload_address = ack_flags;
716: 
717:   if (ack_slots_used() >= MB_ACK_HIGH_WATER)
718:     {
719:       g_probe_requested = true;
720:     }
721: 
722:   (void)dispatch_locked();
723:   return OK;
724: }

726: static int mailbox_rx(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
727: {
728:   irqstate_t flags;
729:   uint8_t control;
730: 
731:   flags = up_irq_save();
732:   g_stats.rx++;
733:   control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
734: 
735:   if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET) != 0)
736:     {
737:       if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX) == 0 ||
738:           (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) & 0xf0u) != 0x40u ||
739:           (control & ~(BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0)
740:         {
741:           g_stats.bad_header++;
742:         }
743:       else
744:         {
745:           g_stats.resets++;
746:           begin_abort(-ECONNRESET);
747:         }
748:     }
749:   else if ((control & BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX) != 0)
750:     {
751:       handle_ack(message);
752:     }
753:   else
754:     {
755:       int ret = handle_command(message);
756: 
757:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
758:         {
759:           up_irq_restore(flags);
760:           return ret;
761:         }
762:     }
763: 
764:   up_irq_restore(flags);
765:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
766:   return OK;
767: }

813:   (void)argc;
814:   (void)argv;

816:   for (;;)
817:     {
818:       struct active_transaction *probe;
819:       irqstate_t flags;
820:       bool request_probe;
821: 
822:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_tx_sem, MB_WORK_INTERVAL);
823:       flags = up_irq_save();
824: 
825:       probe = busy_probe();
826:       if ((g_active.busy &&
827:            clock_systime_ticks() - g_active.started >= MB_TIMEOUT) ||
828:           (probe != NULL &&
829:            clock_systime_ticks() - probe->started >= MB_TIMEOUT))
830:         {
831:           g_stats.timeout++;
832:           if (probe != NULL)
833:             {
834:               probe->quarantine = true;
835:               complete_transaction(probe, NULL, -ETIMEDOUT);
836:               g_stats.probe_fail++;
837:               set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN);
838:             }
839:           else
840:             {
841:               begin_abort(-ETIMEDOUT);
842:             }
843:         }
844: 
845:       if (g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_DOWN &&
846:           clock_systime_ticks() - g_down_since >= MB_DOWN_RETRY)
847:         {
848:           select_recovery_epoch();
849:         }
850: 
851:       (void)dispatch_locked();
852:       if (g_probe_requested && ack_slots_used() < MB_ACK_HIGH_WATER)
853:         {
854:           g_probe_requested = false;
855:         }
856: 
857:       request_probe = g_probe_requested &&
858:                       g_link_state == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY &&
859:                       !g_channels[4].queued && !g_active.busy;
860:       if (request_probe)
861:         {
862:           g_probe_requested = false;
863:         }
864: 
865:       up_irq_restore(flags);
866: 
867:       if (request_probe)
868:         {
869:           bk7258_mb_uart_request_state();
870:         }
871:     }
872: 
873:   return OK;

89:   if (errors != 0)
90:     {
91:       putreg32((config & MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK) | errors, MBOX_CH1_CFG);
92:     }

95: static bool mbox_valid_envelope(uint8_t source, uint32_t address,
96:                                 uint32_t length)
97: {
98:   if (source != 0)
99:     {
100:       g_stats.bad_source++;
101:       return false;
102:     }
103: 
104:   if (length != BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
105:     {
106:       g_stats.bad_length++;
107:       return false;
108:     }
109: 
110:   if ((address & 3u) != 0 || address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START ||
111:       address > BK7258_CP_RAM_END - BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
112:     {
113:       g_stats.bad_address++;
114:       return false;
115:     }
116: 
117:   return true;
118: }

120: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
121: {
122:   uintptr_t status;
123: 
124:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
125:     {
126:       return -EINVAL;
127:     }
128: 
129:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
130:    * receive FIFO status register.
131:    */
132: 
133:   status = destination == 0 ? MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
134:            destination == 1 ? MBOX_CH1_STATUS : MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
135:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
136:     {
137:       return -EAGAIN;
138:     }
139: 
140:   putreg32(data[0], MBOX_CH1_TDATA0);
141:   putreg32(data[1], MBOX_CH1_TDATA1);
142:   putreg32(destination, MBOX_CH1_TID);

146: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_alloc_desc(void)
147: {
148:   unsigned int i;
149: 
150:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
151:     {
152:       if (!g_rx_desc[i].used)
153:         {
154:           return &g_rx_desc[i];
155:         }
156:     }
157: 
158:   return NULL;
159: }
160: 
161: static bool mbox_priority_message(
162:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
163: {
164:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
165: 
166:   return (control & (BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0;
167: }
168: 
169: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_oldest_desc(bool priority)
170: {
171:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *oldest = NULL;
172:   unsigned int i;
173: 
174:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
175:     {
176:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc = &g_rx_desc[i];
177: 
178:       if (!desc->used || mbox_priority_message(&desc->message) != priority)
179:         {
180:           continue;
181:         }
182: 
183:       if (oldest == NULL || (int32_t)(desc->order - oldest->order) < 0)
184:         {
185:           oldest = desc;
186:         }
187:     }
188: 
189:   return oldest;
190: }

192: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
193: {
194:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
195:   int ret;
196: 
197:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
198:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
199:    */
200: 
201:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
202:     {
203:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
204:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
205:         {
206:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
207:           break;
208:         }
209: 
210:       desc->used = false;
211:     }
212: 
213:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
214:     {
215:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
216:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
217:         {
218:           break;
219:         }
220: 
221:       desc->used = false;
222:     }
223: }
224: 
225: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
226: {
227:   (void)irq;
228:   (void)context;
229:   (void)arg;
230: 
231:   mbox_clear_errors();
232: 
233:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0)
234:     {
235:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
236:       uint32_t address;
237:       uint32_t length;
238:       uint8_t source;
239: 
240:       mbox_process_desc();
241:       desc = mbox_alloc_desc();
242:       if (desc == NULL)
243:         {
244:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
245:           break;
246:         }
247: 
248:       source = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_SID) & 0x0fu;
249:       address = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_RDATA0);
250:       length = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_RDATA1);
251:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
252:         {
253:           continue;
254:         }
255: 
256:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
257:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
258:              sizeof(desc->message));
259:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
260:       desc->used = true;
261:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
262:       mbox_process_desc();
263:     }
264: 
265:   mbox_process_desc();
266: 
267:   return OK;
268: }

270: void bk7258_mbox_set_callback(bk7258_mbox_callback_t callback)
271: {
272:   g_callback = callback;
273: }

276: {
277:   irqstate_t flags;
278: 
279:   if (stats == NULL)
280:     {
281:       return;
282:     }
283: 
284:   flags = up_irq_save();
285:   *stats = g_stats;
286:   up_irq_restore(flags);
287: }

289: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)
290: {
291:   int ret;
292: 
293:   if (g_mbox_ready)
294:     {
295:       return OK;
296:     }
297: 
298:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));
299:   g_rx_order = 0;
300:   memset(&g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
301: 
302:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and
303:    * descriptors before enabling the route; pre-existing FIFO entries are
304:    * then processed normally instead of being blindly discarded.
305:    */
306: 
307:   putreg32(2u | MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
308:            MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN, MBOX_CH1_CFG);
309:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG);
310:   modifyreg32(MBOX_CTRL, 0, 1u << 2);
311:   mbox_clear_errors();
312: 
313:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_irq, NULL);
314:   if (ret < 0)
315:     {
316:       return ret;
317:     }
318: 
319:   g_mbox_ready = true;
320:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);
321:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
322:   return OK;
323: }

100: ## 3. 正确构建链条
101: 
102: 最终固件链条固定为：
103: 
104: ```text
105: OpenVela nuttx.bin
106:   -> bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
107:   -> EXTERNAL_AP_BIN
108:   -> package/tmp/app1.bin
109:   -> package/all-app.bin
110: 
111: Armino CP app.bin + Beken bootloader.bin
112:   ---------------------------------------> package/all-app.bin
113: ```
114: 
115: 修改以下任一输入后，不得直接做 SMP 增量构建：
116: 
117: - `ram_regions.csv`
118: - AP/CP `config`
119: - Kconfig 默认值
120: - 分区生成脚本
121: - SoC 链接脚本
122: 
123: 原因是顶层 `partitions/ram_regions.h` 可以先更新，而 AP/CP CMake 构建目录中的
124: `armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv`、生成头和预处理链接脚本仍可能保留旧值。
125: 这会形成顶层 16 MiB、核内仍 8 MiB 的不一致产物。
126: 
127: 先构建 OpenVela AP，并将输入放到 SMP 工作树：
128: 
129: ```bash
130: cd ~/vela_competition/contest
131: ./build.sh \
132:   vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh \
133:   -e -Werror --cmake -j8
134: 
135: cp \
136:   cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin \
137:   ~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
138: ```
139: 
140: 然后执行项目级 clean 和容器内完整构建：
141: 
142: ```bash
143: cd ~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp
144: make -C projects/app_ab clean
145: 
146: podman run --rm \
147:   --userns=keep-id \
148:   -v "$PWD:/armino" \
149:   -w /armino \
150:   localhost/bekencorp/armino-idk:1.5 \
151:   make -C projects/app_ab bk7258 \
152:   SDK_DIR=/armino \
153:   EXTERNAL_AP_BIN=/armino/build/openvela-ap.bin
154: ```
155: 
156: `make -C projects/app_ab clean`只删除`projects/app_ab/build`，不会删除
157: `build/openvela-ap.bin`。仅安装 Podman 时不要使用内部调用 Docker 的`dbuild.sh`。
158: 
159: ## 4. 构建验收
160: 
161: 以下文件必须都反映同一份 16 MiB 布局：
162: 
163: ```text
164: projects/app_ab/partitions/bk7258/ram_regions.csv
165: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/partitions/ram_regions.h
166: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv
167: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258_ap/armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv
168: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/bk7258/bk7258_out.ld
169: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258_ap/armino/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap_out.ld
170: ```
171: 
172: 关键值应为：
173: 
174: ```text
175: CONFIG_PSRAM_CAPACITY          0x01000000
176: CP_PSRAM_HEAP                 0x60700000 + 0x00020000
177: AP_PSRAM_HEAP                 0x60720000 + 0x002e0000
178: AP_PSRAM_SECTION              0x60a00000 + 0x00600000
179: PSRAM 最终边界                0x61000000

text:
**Executive Finding**

The reproducible failure is caused by a proven 32-bit overflow in NuttX’s generic architecture-timer conversion on the AP:

```c
return TICK2USEC(timebase) + (status.timeout - status.timeleft);
```

Although `current_usec()` returns `uint64_t`, `timebase` is a 32-bit `clock_t` in this configuration and `TICK2USEC(timebase)` multiplies by `1000L` in 32-bit arithmetic. AP time therefore jumps backward every `2^32` microseconds, not at the normal 32-bit millisecond/tick wrap.

The heartbeat thread has a relative `nxsig_usleep(2000000)` watchdog deadline outstanding across that backward jump. Its absolute deadline is then above the maximum value AP time can reach before the same premature jump repeats. The thread remains blocked indefinitely, AP heartbeats stop, and CP asserts after its compiled 6,000 ms heartbeat timeout.

The reported CP uptime, approximately `8,594,500 ms`, is within `4,565.408 ms` of the predicted boundary after accounting for the AP SysTick running at approximately half its configured rate. The 120 MHz/60 MHz discrepancy is supported strongly by the CP frequency configuration and exact timing, but the actual clock register was not captured, so that scaling explanation is high-confidence rather than directly measured.

Confidence:

- AP timer arithmetic overflow and blocked heartbeat mechanism: **>99%**
- Explanation of the 2x wall-time scale by CPU1 running at 60 MHz while AP SysTick assumes 120 MHz: **95%**
- Mailbox corruption, queue exhaustion, or low-voltage powerdown as the initiating cause: **<5%**

No files were modified.

**Build And Source Provenance**

The contest manifest links the project-owned BK7258 port into the OpenVela tree at [contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing.xml](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing.xml:15). The actual paths used by OpenVela resolve back to the contest project-owned copies.

The AP chip CMake list includes both the timer and heartbeat/PWC source:

- [CMakeLists.txt](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/CMakeLists.txt:7): `bk7258_timerisr.c`
- [CMakeLists.txt](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/CMakeLists.txt:17): `bk7258_pm_pwc.c`

The retained OpenVela compile database confirms compilation from the linked paths:

- [compile_commands.json](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/compile_commands.json:240): timer source
- [compile_commands.json](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/compile_commands.json:290): heartbeat/PWC source
- [compile_commands.json](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/compile_commands.json:500): NuttX `arch_timer.c`
- [compile_commands.json](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/compile_commands.json:6255): board bring-up source

The intended package chain is documented at [README.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:100):

```text
OpenVela nuttx.bin
 -> bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
 -> EXTERNAL_AP_BIN
 -> package/tmp/app1.bin
 -> package/all-app.bin
```

The currently packaged AP inputs are internally consistent:

```text
bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin                 SHA256 133cf4b8...
projects/app_ab/build/.../package/tmp/app1.bin    SHA256 133cf4b8...
```

That hash matches the package record at [README.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:223), and the final `all-app.bin` is the documented `93e540db...`.

There is, however, an AP provenance gap: the currently retained `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin` now hashes to `e2c94abc...`, not `133cf4b8...`. It was rebuilt after the packaged AP was copied. Consequently, its map is representative of the same defect but is not the exact map for the packaged AP image.

The packaged `openvela-ap.bin` itself contains:

- The exact string `heartbeat worker started, interval=2000 ms`
- A unique Thumb instruction signature at binary offset `0x56c4` corresponding to a 32-bit multiply by 1000 with the returned high word set to zero

Thus the faulty timer conversion is present in the packaged AP even though its original matching map is no longer retained.

**AP Heartbeat Path**

The visible boot log is emitted at [bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:64). It reports successful thread creation; it is not emitted by each heartbeat.

The worker is [bk7258_pm_pwc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:70):

- Line 78: `nxsig_usleep(2000000)`
- Line 79: sends IPC command `2` on logical channel `0x10`
- Lines 80-81: supplies a 4-byte payload, satisfying CP’s payload-length check
- Line 205: creates `ipc-heartbeat` at priority 100

IPC command `2` is `IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION`, defined at [mb_ipc_cmd.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.h:29).

The AP message wrapper is at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1105), and it queues through `bk7258_mailbox_send_wire()` at line 1118.

The logical transport permits only one queued message per channel and can return `-EBUSY` or `-ENOLINK` at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:957). The heartbeat worker ignores that return value. This is a robustness defect, but it does not explain the deterministic uptime boundary.

The physical mailbox checks FIFO-full and returns `-EAGAIN` at [bk7258_mbox0.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:120). No mailbox counter, sequence number, slot count, or FIFO depth has a period near 8.59 million milliseconds.

**CP Timeout And Assert Path**

The current authoritative mirror and working-tree CP heartbeat sources are byte-identical:

- [contest mirror](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:24)
- [build working tree](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:24)

Relevant CP behavior:

- [mb_ipc_heartbeat.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:32): nominal heartbeat interval 2,000 ms
- Line 33: tests `CONFIG_WDT_EN`
- Line 36: otherwise chooses `3 * 2000 = 6000 ms`
- Line 113: timeout calculation
- Lines 129-136: explicit wrap-aware unsigned subtraction
- Line 138: compares elapsed time against the timeout
- Line 140: refreshes the timestamp for an on-time heartbeat
- Lines 144-155: grants a timeout exemption after low-voltage resume
- Line 237: waits for heartbeat/control events
- Lines 289-298: logs timeout, marks link down, and asserts
- Line 293: emits `IPC[%d]heartbeat timeout %d,%d`
- Line 298: exact asserted source line
- Line 338: heartbeat notification sets the event flag

The CP IPC command dispatcher verifies a payload of at least four bytes and calls the heartbeat notifier at [mb_ipc_cmd.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:666).

The generated CP config contains `CONFIG_INT_WDT=1` and `CONFIG_INT_WDT_PERIOD_MS=8000` at [sdkconfig.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/config/sdkconfig.h:190), but it does not define `CONFIG_WDT_EN`. Therefore the heartbeat code compiles the 6,000 ms fallback, not 8,000 ms.

This is confirmed directly in `app.elf`: the linked `mb_ipc_task` loads literal `6000`, calls `ap_console_bridge_link_down()`, and passes literal `298` to the assert output function. The reported `mb_ipc_task:298` therefore matches the linked CP binary exactly.

CP `rtos_get_time()` is a 32-bit 1 kHz FreeRTOS tick converted to milliseconds at [rtos_pub.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_rtos/freertos/v10/rtos_pub.c:1174). Its own comment says it wraps after about 49.7 days. At 2h23m it is nowhere near overflow, and the heartbeat subtraction handles that eventual wrap correctly.

**NuttX Timer Defect**

The AP initializes SysTick through [bk7258_timerisr.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:13), passing `CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ` at line 16.

The generic architecture timer stores elapsed ticks in `clock_t timebase` at [arch_timer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:49). In non-tickless mode, it increments that value once per SysTick at line 187.

The faulty conversion is [arch_timer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:97):

```c
static uint64_t current_usec(void)
{
  ...
  return TICK2USEC(timebase) + (status.timeout - status.timeleft);
}
```

`TICK2USEC` is defined at [clock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/clock.h:168):

```c
#define TICK2USEC(tick) ((tick) * USEC_PER_TICK)
```

`USEC_PER_TICK` becomes `1000L` at [clock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/clock.h:127). Because `clock_t` is 32-bit here, the multiplication overflows before conversion to the function’s `uint64_t` return type.

The compiled AP object proves this:

```text
mov.w r3, #1000
movs  r1, #0          ; high 32 bits of uint64 return forced to zero
mla   r0, r3, r5, r0 ; only low 32-bit product retained
```

`up_timer_gettick()` divides that already-overflowed value by 1000 at [arch_timer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:265). Because `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH=y`, `clock_systime_ticks()` explicitly takes this path at [clock_systime_ticks.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/clock/clock_systime_ticks.c:89).

**Why The Thread Never Wakes**

`nxsig_usleep()` converts 2,000,000 microseconds to a two-second `timespec` at [sig_usleep.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/signal/sig_usleep.c:70), then calls `nxsig_nanosleep()` at line 82.

`nxsig_clockwait()` converts the delay to ticks and creates an absolute watchdog deadline at [sig_timedwait.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/signal/sig_timedwait.c:305). It then removes the heartbeat thread from the runnable list and blocks it at lines 323-334.

The deadline is:

```c
clock() + delay + 1
```

from [clock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/clock.h:371).

Immediately before the premature timer jump, AP time approaches approximately tick `4,294,967`. A two-second sleep can therefore be armed with an absolute expiration around tick `4,296,000`.

But the faulty AP clock never reaches that value. It jumps from approximately `4,294,967` back to zero whenever the 32-bit microsecond product wraps, then repeats the same sawtooth.

Watchdog expiry uses wrap-aware `clock_compare()` at [wd_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/wdog/wd_start.c:136), defined at [clock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/clock.h:545). Normal 32-bit tick wrap is handled correctly, but this is not a normal `clock_t` wrap: the clock jumps early at only about 4.3 million ticks while the deadline remains a valid 32-bit value above that artificial maximum. Consequently, that deadline can never compare as reached. The heartbeat thread remains blocked indefinitely.

The mailbox worker’s repeated 10 ms semaphore sleeps use the same watchdog clock and can also become stranded near the boundary. That can worsen transport recovery, but the heartbeat sleep alone is sufficient to trigger the CP assertion.

**Timing Calculation**

With `CONFIG_USEC_PER_TICK=1000`, the conversion wraps when:

```text
timebase * 1000 = 2^32 microseconds
timebase         = 4,294,967.296 AP ticks
nominal time     = 4,294,967.296 ms
                 = 4,294.967296 s
                 = 1h 11m 34.967296s
```

The reported failure is:

```text
8,594,500 ms = 8,594.5 s = 2h 23m 14.5s
```

If the physical SysTick interval is 2 ms rather than the configured 1 ms:

```text
2^32 us * 2 = 8,589,934.592 ms
             = 2h 23m 09.934592s
```

Difference from the observed assert:

```text
8,594,500 - 8,589,934.592 = 4,565.408 ms
```

At the same 2x clock scale, AP’s nominal 2-second heartbeat arrives about every 4 wall-clock seconds. CP’s linked timeout is 6 seconds. Depending on heartbeat phase, the expected assert is approximately 2 to 6 seconds after the AP timer jump. The observed `4.565408 s` is inside that window.

This correspondence is much tighter than expected from an unrelated scheduler, mailbox, or PM failure.

**120 MHz Versus 60 MHz**

AP hardcodes 120 MHz:

- [Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/Kconfig:15): fixed CPU1 frequency
- [Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/Kconfig:17): default `120000000`
- [final AP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:230): `CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ=120000000`
- [bk7258_timerisr.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:16): passes that value to SysTick

CP is configured to lower the shared clocks to 60 MHz:

- [CP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config:928): `CONFIG_CPU_DEFAULT_FREQ_60M=y`
- [bk_init.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_init/bk_init.c:372): votes the default module to 60 MHz after initialization
- [sys_hal.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/sys_hal.c:623): 60 MHz case explicitly covers CPU0, CPU1, CPU2, and bus
- [pm.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_pm/pm.c:2218): global maximum frequency-vote selection and clock switch

The AP port explicitly says runtime DVFS is unsupported, yet CP owns and changes the shared clock. No AP SysTick frequency-change callback exists. The exact factor-of-two failure timing is therefore strong evidence that CPU1 is physically at 60 MHz while SysTick reload calculations assume 120 MHz.

A register capture or GPIO-period measurement around SysTick/heartbeat is still required to call this directly measured rather than inferred.

**SYSTEM_TIME64 Evidence**

The final AP config explicitly disables it at [`.config`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:396).

Without it, `clock_t` and `time_t` are 32-bit at [sys/types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/sys/types.h:254). With `CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64=y`, `clock_t` becomes `uint64_t`, so `timebase * 1000L` is promoted to 64-bit arithmetic and the premature microsecond-product wrap disappears.

NuttX documents the option as the 64-bit system-clock mode at [sched/Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/Kconfig:194). The same Kconfig also provides overflow correction only when `SYSTEM_TIME64` is enabled at line 306.

This is the smallest project-owned correction because the board defconfig is owned by the contest project and no upstream NuttX edit is required.

**Power Management Assessment**

AP-side NuttX PM is disabled at [`.config`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:755). RTC and clock-timekeeping are also disabled at lines 595 and 398. AP therefore has no NuttX low-power clock resynchronization involved in this event.

CP PM and FreeRTOS tickless idle are enabled at [CP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config:252) and line 279.

However:

- `CONFIG_PM_AP_POWERDOWN_WHEN_LV` is disabled at [CP config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config:950).
- `CONFIG_PM_LV_SUBCORES_ON` is enabled at line 947.
- CP’s heartbeat low-voltage callback resets the heartbeat timestamp after resume at [mb_ipc_heartbeat.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:196).
- The low-voltage state check at line 144 suppresses one timeout rather than creating one.

PM can alter the CPU clock and therefore contributes to the SysTick frequency mismatch, but there is no deterministic PM timeout or powerdown interval near `2^32 us * 2`.

**Stale CP Artifact Evidence**

The CP build rule uses `/armino/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c` at [build.ninja](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/build.ninja:3539), and the compile database confirms that source at [compile_commands.json](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/compile_commands.json:1433).

Timestamps show:

```text
CP heartbeat object:  2026-08-04 00:02:16
CP app.elf:           2026-08-04 20:33:53
Current CP source:    2026-08-04 20:40:24
```

Thus `app.elf` and its object predate the current source bytes and cannot be claimed as a fresh rebuild of the current work tree.

For the relevant path, binary evidence is nevertheless conclusive:

- DWARF maps `mb_ipc_task` to current-style source line 220.
- The binary includes `ap_console_bridge_link_down()`.
- It embeds assert line 298.
- It uses a literal 6,000 ms timeout.

Therefore the stale-build issue is a reproducibility problem, but it does not undermine the timeout diagnosis. The exact complete source hash used to produce the object cannot be reconstructed from the retained artifacts.

**Secondary Issues, Not Root Cause**

- The heartbeat send result is ignored at [bk7258_pm_pwc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:79). Repeated `-EBUSY` or `-ENOLINK` could independently cause a timeout under transport stress.
- `CONFIG_WDT_EN` versus actual `CONFIG_INT_WDT` makes the CP heartbeat timeout 6 seconds instead of the apparently intended 8 seconds.
- At the current 60/120 mismatch, heartbeats are approximately 4 seconds apart, leaving only about 2 seconds of CP timeout margin.
- AP mailbox timeout and worker timing use the same defective clock, so transport recovery can also stall at the arithmetic boundary.
- CP low-voltage handling has two exemption paths, but neither explains the power-of-two timing.
- No raw board log containing the supplied timestamp was found in the workspace; the numerical comparison uses the timestamp from the request.

**Minimal Fix**

The smallest mandatory project-owned fix is:

```text
CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64=y
```

in:

[defconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:100)

This changes `clock_t`, `timebase`, the multiplication, watchdog deadlines, and signed wrap comparisons coherently. A local cast in the heartbeat worker or replacing `nxsig_usleep()` would only hide one symptom.

A strongly recommended companion fix is to establish one clock owner:

- Either keep CPU1 at 120 MHz while OpenVela AP is running through a CP `PM_DEV_ID_CPU1` frequency vote, releasing it on CPU1 shutdown.
- Or configure AP SysTick for the actual stable 60 MHz clock.
- If runtime DVFS must remain enabled, update/rebase SysTick whenever CP changes CPU1 clock, or move AP scheduling to a clock source independent of core frequency.

Pinning CPU1 at 120 MHz is the least disruptive companion to the current AP configuration. Simply changing the AP constant to 60 MHz is insufficient if other CP modules later raise the shared clock.

The CP conditional should separately be corrected to use the real watchdog symbol, likely `CONFIG_INT_WDT`, but increasing the timeout is mitigation, not a root fix.

**Test Matrix**

1. Perform a clean OpenVela and clean `app_ab` build. Require identical hashes for `cmake_out/.../nuttx.bin`, `build/openvela-ap.bin`, and `package/tmp/app1.bin`.

2. Verify generated AP config contains `CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64=y`. Disassemble `current_usec()` and confirm a 64-bit multiply/add sequence rather than a low-word-only `mla`.

3. Pre-fix accelerated reproduction: with a debugger, seed `g_timer.timebase` just below `floor(UINT32_MAX / 1000)` and verify that a two-second heartbeat sleep crossing the boundary remains blocked.

4. Post-fix accelerated boundary test: seed the 64-bit `g_timer.timebase` around the former `2^32 us` boundary and verify monotonic `clock_systime_ticks()`, continuous heartbeats, and no CP timeout.

5. Seed near `UINT32_MAX` ticks as a second post-fix test, validating that 64-bit time crosses the former normal 32-bit tick wrap.

6. Measure physical heartbeat spacing and SysTick with CPU1 at 60 MHz and 120 MHz. Expected healthy spacing is approximately 2 wall seconds after clock ownership is fixed.

7. Exercise CP frequency transitions `120 -> 60 -> 120` while AP is active. Either prohibit them through the CPU1 vote or verify SysTick is reprogrammed without lost/early watchdogs.

8. Run a minimum 3-hour idle soak. This crosses the observed failure point with margin.

9. Repeat the 3-hour soak under Wi-Fi traffic, camera/media activity, UART bridge traffic, and maximum scheduler load.

10. Force CP low-voltage entry/exit repeatedly. Verify AP remains powered, CP’s resume exemption behaves once per resume, and heartbeat cadence recovers immediately.

11. Inject mailbox FIFO-full, delayed ACK, dropped ACK, reset, and `-EBUSY` conditions. Add heartbeat send-result counters/logging before this test so sleep failure and transport rejection are distinguishable.

12. Verify the CP binary after a clean build still maps the intended assert line and inspect whether the timeout literal is 6,000 or 8,000 ms according to the corrected config symbol.

The acceptance condition should be continuous AP heartbeat delivery across both accelerated timer boundaries, all frequency/PM transitions, and at least one 3-hour real-time soak, with no `hrt` timeout, mailbox recovery loop, or blocked `ipc-heartbeat` thread.
